content.value_statement: Crypto exchanges need reliable ways to find qualified token listing prospects. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured patterns for scoring, wallet review, paid-source use, and human-approved outreach.
actual_capabilities: Outlines intelligence source categories for token discovery across DEX data, social signals, safety checks, and forums.
Defines a 100-point token scoring framework with liquidity, market cap, volume, social, age, and team factors.
Describes wallet forensics steps for deployer funding, balances, transfer history, identity, and score adjustments.
Maps a ten-stage business development pipeline from discovery through listing negotiation.
Recommends human approval before outreach and verified endpoints for x402 payments.
limitations: It provides patterns and operating rules, not a runnable agent implementation.
It does not verify market data, token safety, or exchange compliance by itself.
It does not replace legal, security, or financial review for crypto listing decisions.
It assumes users can validate external data sources and payment endpoints.

use_cases.title: Exchange Listing Research
use_cases.description: A listing manager can structure daily token discovery, qualification, and outreach approval work.

use_cases.title: Crypto Data Pipeline Design

use_cases.title: Due Diligence Workflow

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Token Scoring Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a simple token listing scoring plan for a crypto exchange. Include factors, weights, and rejection rules.

prompt_templates.title: Design Daily Discovery Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a daily prospect discovery workflow. Prioritize free sources, confirmations, and human approval points.

prompt_templates.title: Review Wallet Forensics Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate wallet forensics criteria for token deployers. Identify required checks, positive flags, and rejection flags.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Agent Architecture Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to produce an architecture brief for a crypto BD agent. Cover source routing, model cascade, payment controls, agent identity, pipeline stages, and audit logs.

output_examples.input: Plan a listing qualification workflow for a new exchange.
output: A daily process that starts with free token discovery sources.
A scoring checklist covering liquidity, market cap, volume, social activity, age, and team transparency.
Human approval before outreach and a log for paid source usage.

output_examples.input: Review a token prospect that scored above 70.
output: A wallet forensics checklist for deployer funding, balances, transfers, and identity signals.
Positive flags for clean wallets, institutional backing, and verified authority status.
Rejection flags for mixer funding, exploit history, and severe dump patterns.

output_examples.input: Prepare guidance for using paid intelligence sources.
output: A free-first sourcing plan with paid calls reserved for high-signal checks.
Budget controls for daily x402 usage.
ROI logging for each paid source call.

best_practices: Cross-check every prospect with at least two independent sources before scoring it as qualified.
Require human approval before sending outreach or making external commitments.
Keep payment wallets, on-chain posting wallets, and model routing credentials separate.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on token names without verified contract and pair addresses.
Do not automate outreach without human approval and clear compliance boundaries.
Do not send funds or use paid endpoints before verifying endpoint trust.

faq.question: Does this skill build a trading bot?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on business development workflows for token listings, not trading decisions or automated execution.

faq.question: Can it run the reference implementation?
faq.answer: No. The skill links to a reference project, but this package only provides guidance.

faq.question: Does it collect private keys?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly warns users never to share API keys or wallet private keys.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What external services does it mention?
faq.answer: It discusses DEX data, safety checks, wallet forensics tools, web scraping services, x402 endpoints, and ERC-8004 identity services.

faq.question: How should paid data sources be handled?
faq.answer: Use free data first, verify paid endpoints, set budget limits, and log ROI for every paid call.
